exposure: Surfactant administration through a thin endotracheal catheter (TEC) during spontaneous breathing
outcome: Frequency and duration of mechanical ventilation requirement
Duration of nasal continuous positive airway pressure (NCPAP) requirement
Duration of infants' stay in neonatal intensive care unit
Frequency and severity of intraventricular hemorrhage of the brain
cohort: The study included 40 premature infants with a gestational age of <32 weeks and birth weight of <1500g suffering from Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) who needed surfactant administration.
finding: The TEC method significantly decreased mechanical ventilation requirement compared to the INSURE method, while NCPAP requirement and duration of hospitalization did not significantly differ between the groups.
